stem: A patient develops an erythematous, pruritic rash confined to areas exposed to a detergent. Which mechanism BEST distinguishes irritant contact dermatitis from allergic contact dermatitis?
options: Delayed T-cell hypersensitivity requiring prior sensitization
Direct epidermal injury without prior sensitization

stem: A nurse suspects allergic contact dermatitis rather than irritant dermatitis. Which historical feature is MOST supportive?
options: Immediate burning after first exposure to a strong acid
A rash limited only to pressure points
A previous sensitizing exposure followed by a delayed eczematous reaction
Absence of pruritus with chemical exposure

stem: Which exposure listed in the material is a COMMON trigger of contact dermatitis?
A patient with suspected allergic contact dermatitis undergoes diagnostic testing. Which test is MOST appropriate?
options: Skin biopsy as first-line for every case

stem: A patient develops dermatitis only after exposure to a topical substance followed by sunlight. Which test best evaluates this pattern?
Which finding is MOST characteristic of acute contact dermatitis?
options: Erythema with vesicles or oozing and intense pruritus
Well-demarcated silvery plaques on extensor surfaces
Deep painless nodules with central necrosis

stem: A patient with chronic contact dermatitis has lichenification. Which pathophysiologic process BEST explains this finding?
options: Repeated rubbing and scratching causing epidermal thickening

stem: Which nursing intervention is MOST appropriate for acute weeping contact dermatitis?
options: Encourage vigorous scratching to remove scales
Use soothing wet compresses as prescribed and avoid the offending agent
Apply potent irritant cleansers to dry the lesion

stem: Which statement about topical corticosteroids for dermatitis is MOST accurate based on the text?
options: Apply thickly over normal surrounding skin to prevent spread
Apply a thin layer to affected areas and avoid excessive prolonged use because of adverse effects
Use without regard to skin integrity or infection
Discontinue after one dose if itching persists

stem: A patient with dermatitis asks why avoiding the offending substance is emphasized even when topical therapy is effective. Which response is BEST?
options: Topical therapy permanently prevents future reactions
Ongoing exposure can perpetuate inflammation despite symptomatic treatment
Exposure has no influence once medication is started
Avoidance is useful only in fungal disease

stem: Which statement BEST characterizes psoriasis?
options: A chronic noninfectious inflammatory skin disorder with markedly accelerated epidermal cell turnover
A fungal infection limited to intertriginous regions
A purely allergic disease caused by histamine alone

stem: The epidermal turnover rate in psoriasis is described as being approximately how much faster than normal?
Which lesion pattern is MOST typical of psoriasis?
options: Diffuse urticaria with transient wheals only
Well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scales
Single black eschar with surrounding edema

stem: Which body sites are classically associated with psoriasis in the material?
options: Extensor surfaces, scalp, and lumbosacral region

stem: A patient with psoriasis develops pinpoint bleeding when scales are removed. Which sign is being described?
Which factor is listed as a possible precipitant of psoriasis exacerbation?
options: Low environmental temperature as the sole cause

stem: Which medication class may trigger or worsen psoriasis according to the text?
A patient with chronic psoriasis suddenly develops diffuse erythema involving most of the body surface with fever and fluid imbalance. Which complication is MOST likely?
Why is erythrodermic psoriasis clinically dangerous?
options: Extensive skin involvement can impair thermoregulation and fluid-electrolyte balance
It permanently suppresses all sweat glands

stem: Which complication is associated with psoriasis and involves the joints?
Which treatment in the text is used to slow excessive epidermal turnover in psoriasis?
Why should systemic corticosteroids be used cautiously in psoriasis?
options: Withdrawal may precipitate severe flare or erythrodermic disease
They are the only safe first-line treatment

stem: Which phototherapy modality is described for psoriasis management?
options: No light-based therapy is ever used
Narrow-band UVB or PUVA depending on regimen

stem: A patient receiving systemic retinoid therapy for psoriasis should receive which critical counseling?
options: Increase alcohol intake to improve absorption
Strict pregnancy avoidance because of teratogenicity

stem: Which adverse effect is associated with systemic retinoids such as acitretin?
options: Guaranteed renal failure after one dose

stem: A patient with mild localized psoriasis asks why emollients are prescribed. Which explanation is BEST?
options: They reduce dryness and scaling and improve barrier comfort

stem: Which statement BEST differentiates psoriasis from impetigo?
options: Both are caused exclusively by fungi
Psoriasis is always bacterial and impetigo is autoimmune
Psoriasis is chronic and noninfectious, whereas impetigo is a contagious bacterial infection

stem: Which description is MOST characteristic of impetigo?
options: Deep ulcers with black necrotic centers
Generalized wheals that resolve within hours
Vesicles or pustules that rupture and form honey-colored crusts

stem: Impetigo in children commonly affects which area?
options: Face, especially around the nose and mouth

stem: Why are antibiotics used in impetigo even though some cases may resolve spontaneously?
options: They shorten disease duration and reduce transmission
They are used only for pain control

stem: A child with impetigo has spreading lesions and household contacts at risk. Which nursing priority is MOST appropriate?
options: Cover all lesions with occlusive plastic indefinitely
Reinforce hygiene and reduce direct sharing/contact to limit spread
Stop antibiotics once lesions appear dry

stem: The epidermis is composed primarily of what type of tissue?
Which epidermal cells are chiefly responsible for producing keratin?
Which cells produce melanin that contributes to skin pigmentation?
Differences in skin color among individuals are attributed mainly to differences in which melanocyte-related factor?
options: Complete absence or presence of epidermis
Size and distribution of melanosomes rather than large differences in melanocyte number

stem: Which structure is NOT normally present on the palms and soles?
Which gland secretes sebum into hair follicles?
Sebum production becomes especially active under the influence of which hormones?
Apocrine sweat glands are most commonly found in which locations?
options: Axillae, areolae, groin, and perineal regions

stem: Apocrine secretions develop characteristic odor mainly because:
options: Skin bacteria act on initially odorless secretions
The secretion is inherently foul before reaching skin

stem: Which layer acts as the principal barrier limiting excessive water loss from the body?
Approximately how much insensible perspiration is described in the text for a normal adult?
Which vitamin-related function is performed by the skin after ultraviolet exposure?
Which mechanism contributes to heat loss by transfer of heat to a cooler object through direct contact?
Which mechanism of heat loss involves bulk movement of air adjacent to the skin?
Which heat-loss mechanism depends on emission of heat to a cooler object at a distance without direct contact?
Heat loss from sweat changing from liquid to vapor is called:
Skin temperature depends strongly on which variable under neural control?
Which autonomic response would MOST directly conserve body heat?
Which response would MOST directly increase heat loss through skin?
During an inflammatory response, histamine can promote which vascular effect?
options: Decreased local blood flow in all tissues

stem: Which inflammatory mediator pair is associated with vasodilation in the material?
Which event is central to acute inflammation after tissue injury?
options: Permanent closure of all local capillaries
Increased vascular permeability allowing plasma proteins and leukocytes into tissues

stem: Which immune components are described as participating in complement-related inflammatory activity?
Bradykinin contributes to inflammation mainly by producing which effect?
Which patient is MOST likely experiencing photoallergic dermatitis rather than phototoxic dermatitis?
options: A patient develops psoriasis after beta-blocker use
A patient develops impetigo after scratching
A previously sensitized person develops an eczematous delayed reaction after a chemical plus sunlight exposure
A patient develops a sunburn-like reaction on first exposure to a photosensitizing chemical

stem: Which description BEST fits phototoxic dermatitis?
options: A nonimmune reaction resembling an exaggerated sunburn after a photosensitizing chemical and light exposure
A delayed T-cell reaction requiring prior sensitization
A chronic plaque disorder with silvery scale

stem: A patient with contact dermatitis is advised to wear cotton clothing and avoid harsh detergents. What is the PRIMARY goal?
options: Reduce irritation, heat retention, and pruritus

stem: Why is a cool, humid environment sometimes recommended for severe dermatitis?
options: It can reduce itching and excessive drying of inflamed skin

stem: Which sign is more strongly associated with psoriasis than contact dermatitis?
options: Linear rash exactly matching an irritant contact area
Immediate burning on first chemical exposure
Vesicular oozing after a new detergent exposure

stem: Which statement is MOST accurate regarding biopsy in psoriasis?
options: Diagnosis is usually clinical; biopsy is rarely needed
Biopsy is mandatory in every patient
Biopsy is used only to diagnose impetigo

stem: Which of the following is a major long-term nursing concern in extensive psoriasis?
options: Monitoring for fluid, electrolyte, and temperature regulation problems

stem: A patient with psoriasis taking acitretin drinks alcohol regularly. Which concern is MOST important?
options: Alcohol converts acitretin into a topical agent
Alcohol use can worsen safety concerns and should be discussed because retinoids have important hepatic and teratogenic risks

stem: A patient with dermatitis has signs of secondary bacterial infection. Which principle is MOST appropriate?
options: Use only emollients regardless of infection severity
Treat the infection while continuing to address the underlying dermatitis and trigger avoidance
Increase exposure to the offending agent to desensitize the skin
Ignore infection because dermatitis is noninfectious

stem: A patient with plaque psoriasis has severe psychosocial distress related to visible lesions. Which nursing intervention BEST addresses the whole-person approach?
options: Provide psychological support alongside skin care and education

stem: Which statement BEST explains why thickened skin can develop in chronic dermatitis?
options: Persistent scratching and rubbing lead to lichenification

stem: A patient develops lesions on the palms and soles that are pustular and recurrent. Which psoriasis variant is MOST consistent?
Which feature MOST strongly favors psoriasis over impetigo in a school-aged child?
options: Chronic recurrent well-demarcated plaques with silvery scale

stem: A nurse is evaluating whether a prescribed dermatitis regimen is working. Which outcome is MOST appropriate?
options: Reduced pruritus, inflammation, and new lesion formation with avoidance of triggers

stem: A patient with extensive psoriasis reports chills, malaise, and worsening generalized erythema after abrupt withdrawal of systemic corticosteroids. Which interpretation is MOST appropriate?
options: The findings indicate normal resolution of psoriasis
The symptoms are best explained by allergic contact dermatitis alone
A severe rebound flare such as erythrodermic psoriasis should be considered
This pattern is typical of uncomplicated impetigo
